title: How Did a Mic Left On Catch Hitler in 1942? 🎙️
description:
The only known recording of Hitler's normal speaking voice exists because a Finnish radio engineer left his microphone running during the Hitler–Mannerheim meeting in June 1942.

Follow Zorbly for a new mystery every day.

#shorts #history #ww2 #finland
pinned_comment: Does hearing him talk calmly make him less scary, or more?
topic: The only recording of Hitler's normal voice (the 1942 Hitler–Mannerheim recording)
script:
This is the only known tape of Hitler not shouting.
You were never supposed to hear it.
June 1942: Hitler visits Finland for Marshal Mannerheim's birthday.
A Finnish engineer records the speeches,
then leaves his mic running.
In a railway car, Hitler just talks.
No shouting.
He admits Soviet factories shocked him.
Eleven minutes in, the SS guards spot the mic.
One draws a finger across his throat.
They want the tape destroyed.
Instead, it's sealed, never to be opened.
Later, actor Bruno Ganz studied it to play him.
So does the calm voice make him less scary, or more?
key_facts: 4 June 1942: Hitler made a secret visit to Finland for Marshal Mannerheim's 75th birthday (Imatra / Immola)
Yle sound engineer Thor Damen kept recording after the official speeches, in Mannerheim's railway carriage, without permission
About 11 minutes were recorded before SS guards noticed and signalled him to stop with a cutthroat gesture
SS demanded the tape be destroyed; Yle kept it in a sealed container promised never to be opened; returned to Yle in 1957, released a few years later
Hitler was shocked by the Red Army's production capability
Bruno Ganz used it to study Hitler's speaking for Downfall (2004)
Described as the only known recording of Hitler speaking in an unofficial tone
